name: milp_direct_integer
steps: Binary variables y_salmon, y_beef, y_pork to select exactly one protein source
Binary variables y_okra, y_carrots, y_celery, y_cabbage to select at least two vegetables
Continuous variables for grams of each food (non-negative)
Link protein selection binary to protein grams: protein_grams <= M * y_X for each protein
Link vegetable selection binary to vegetable grams: veg_grams >= 100 * y_veg (minimum 100g if selected)
Objective: maximize total fiber = 3.2*okra + 2.7*carrots + 1.6*celery + 2*cabbage (scaled per 100g)
Constraints: total weight = 600g, budget <= $15, at least 2 vegetables selected
Use HiGHS highs API: addVariable/addConstr/getSolution. All food-gram vars are continuous (non-negative, can be fractional grams)
Write result to result.json with status/objective_value/objective_bound/runtime_seconds/solution

name: cp_sat_vegetable_protein
steps: Use OR-Tools CP-SAT: boolean variables for protein choice (exactly one of salmon/beef/pork)
Boolean variables for vegetable selection (at least 2 of okra/carrots/celery/cabbage)
Integer variables for grams of each food (0-600, step 1 for grams precision)
Constraints: total grams=600, budget constraint, selection constraints
Objective: maximize fiber content
CP-SAT is robust to the highspy API issues that plagued milp_direct_integer
Write result to result.json with status/objective_value/objective_bound/runtime_seconds/solution

name: milp_binary_then_continuous
steps: Stage 1: Use binary variables to select protein source and at least 2 vegetables via big-M constraints
Stage 2: Once selections fixed, solve continuous allocation problem (linear program) for optimal grams
Binary y_salmon/y_beef/y_pork with sum=1 for protein; binary y_okra/y_carrots/y_celery/y_cabbage with sum>=2 for vegetables
Link binary selections to gram variables with big-M: grams <= 600*y for each food
Objective: maximize fiber; Constraints: total=600g, budget<=15, selection constraints
Two-phase: first solve MILP for selections, then LP for grams given selections
Use HiGHS API: addVariable/addConstr/getSolution
Write result to result.json with status/objective_value/objective_bound/runtime_seconds/solution
